sanskrit: yūpe garte vidveṣaṇaṃ devānāṃ varcasā kṛtam | agnir vām astv antarā yathā vāṃ na sahāsati ||
english: In the post, in the pit, enmity has been made with the radiance of the gods. May fire be between you two, so that you two shall not be together.

sanskrit: yathāhiṃ dveṣṭi puruṣo ahir vā dveṣṭi puruṣam | girir vām astv antarā yathā vāṃ na sahāsati ||
english: As a person hates a serpent, or a serpent hates a person, may a mountain be between you two, so that you two shall not be together.

sanskrit: nānāni vām ākūtāni nānā cittāni santu vām | viṣvañcau pary ā vartethāṃ yathā vāṃ na sahāsati ||
english: May your intentions be different, may your thoughts be different. May you two turn away in opposite directions, so that you two shall not be together.

sanskrit: atra dve kamale dve tuṇḍe na maśīkataṃ taṃ galāpate | bhaṅgalāpato (⟨ bhaṅgurāvato) daha ||
english: Here are two lotuses, two beaks — do not let them touch that one, O lord of the throat. O destroyer, burn him up.

sanskrit: etad yat te yad vā yad vā na cāsan no ca te bhavat | svapne vittaṃ yathā dhanaṃ naśyād id etad etataḥ ||
english: This thing of yours — whether it was or was not, whether it was yours or not — may it perish from here, just as wealth seen in a dream perishes.

sanskrit: āgilo gilāpāpacito gila | naśyād bradhnakam arbhakam ||
english: Swallow, swallow, swallow down the unripened one. May the petty, mean thing perish.

sanskrit: dīrghāyutvāya sahase mahyā ariṣṭatātaye | suparṇo mahyam abravīd etad āśliṣṭabheṣajam ||
english: For long life, for strength, for my wholeness and freedom from harm — the eagle has declared to me: this is the remedy for what clings.

sanskrit: saktūn iva titaünā punanto vidvāṃso vācam akrata | aṅgebhyo viśvāṅgebhyaḥ pra te chinadmy āśliṣṭam ||
english: As the wise ones, purifying meal with a sieve, have fashioned speech — from your limbs, from all your limbs, I cut away that which clings.

sanskrit: avacchindhy āśliṣṭam ūrvā hy asi bheṣajī | divyaḥ suparṇo abravid etad āśliṣṭabheṣajam ||
english: Cut away what clings — for the thigh is a healer. The divine eagle has declared: this is the remedy for what clings.

sanskrit: abhibhūr aham āgamaṃ viśvakarmā svāyudhaḥ | ahaṃ mitrasya kalpayann āsv āśāsu duṣṭaraḥ ||
english: I have come as the overpowering one, as Viśvakarmā, armed with my own weapons. Ordering the affairs of Mitra, I am unconquerable in all these directions.

sanskrit: ahaṃ samityayano ahaṃ viśāṃ purohitaḥ | ahaṃ mitrāṇi kalpayan mayi vāg astu dharṇasī ||
english: I am the one who convenes assemblies; I am the high priest of the clans. Ordering my friendships, may steadfast speech be in me.

sanskrit: ā vaś cakṣur ā vo vācam ā vaḥ samitiṃ dade | yogakṣemaṃ va ādāya- -ahaṃ bhūyāsam uttamaḥ ||
english: I take away your sight, I take away your speech, I take away your assembly. Taking away your welfare and security, may I be supreme.

sanskrit: brahmaṇāgniḥ saṃvidāno rakṣohā nudatām itaḥ | arāyo yas te tanvaṃ durṇāmā yonim āśaye ||
english: Agni, joined with sacred power, the slayer of demons — may he drive away from here the evil-named enemy who lies upon your body and womb.

sanskrit: yas te 'rāyas tanvaṃ durṇāmā yonim āśaye | agniṣ ṭaṃ brahmaṇā yujā rakṣohā nudatām itaḥ ||
english: The evil-named enemy who lies upon your body and womb — may Agni, the slayer of demons, together with his ally sacred power, drive him away from here.

sanskrit: yāny abhvāni rakṣāṃsi ye 'rāyā yātudhānyaḥ | agniṣ ṭvā śagmayā tanvā rakṣohā pātu tebhyaḥ ||
english: From the monstrous demons, from the hostile sorcerers — may Agni, the slayer of demons, protect you with his benevolent body from them.

sanskrit: agniś ca deva savitar iṣam ūrjaṃ dadhānau | pātaṃ mā duścaritād ā mā sucarite bhajataṃ yuvayor avasā sumnam aśīya ||
english: O divine Agni and Savitṛ, bestowing nourishment and vigor — protect me from evil conduct; grant me a share in good conduct. May I attain bliss under your two sheltering graces.

sanskrit: idaṃ tad upa yuva idaṃ tad upa hvaye yac chuśrumā tvat pari | vācaspatir ni yacchatu mayy evāstu mama śrutam ||
english: This very thing I approach you two with, this very thing I invoke — what we have heard coming from you. May the Lord of Speech grant it; may my learning abide in me.

sanskrit: māpatyāya steyaṃ karaṃ mā śrutena vi rādhiṣi | amogham asmākaṃ śrāntam agne draviṇavat kṛdhi ||
english: Let me not steal from my offspring; may I not fail through what I have learned. O Agni, make our toil fruitful, rich in wealth.

sanskrit: madhyameṣṭhā varcasvatyā- -āyuṣe varcase kṛtam | vanuṣva viśvadeveṣu vanuṣva tvaṃ bṛhaspatau ||
english: Standing in the middle, brilliant with radiance — made for life and glory. Win favor among the All-Gods; do you win favor with Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: ghṛtena prajāṃ vanute ghṛtena rayim aśnute | ghṛtenāyuṣyaṃ varcasyaṃ devebhyo vanute pari ||
english: With ghee one wins offspring; with ghee one attains riches. With ghee one wins from the gods what is life-giving and radiance-bestowing.

sanskrit: parjanya pippalās tubhyaṃ nadyo garbhaṃ svastaye | maryādā brahmadevīr āyuṣyaṃ varca āsican ||
english: O Parjanya, the fig-berries — rivers have poured their embryo into you for well-being. The divine boundary-goddesses of sacred power have poured life-giving radiance.

sanskrit: yathā hastī hastinyāḥ padena padam anv agāt | evā tvam aghnye vatsasya padena padam anv ihi ||
english: As a bull elephant follows the footsteps of a cow elephant step by step, so do you, O inviolable cow, follow the footsteps of your calf step by step.

sanskrit: yathā rathasya cakre vi pathaḥ pāṃsum asyathaḥ | evā mano vy asyāmi hṛdayaṃ vananāya kam ||
english: As the two wheels of a chariot scatter the dust of the road, so do I scatter the mind and heart of that one for winning love.

sanskrit: indrasya prathamaṃ vaco devānām aparaṃ vacaḥ | tṛtīyam aśvinor vacas tena gāṃ vānayāmasi ||
english: Indra's is the first word; the gods' is the second word; the Aśvins' is the third word — with that we bring the cow into compliance.

sanskrit: ud itaḥ śyāvau vithurau divaṃ gṛdhrāv iveyathuḥ | śocanāv atiśocanāv asyocchocanau hṛdaḥ ||
english: Up from here, the two dark, trembling ones have gone aloft like two vultures to the sky — the two scorching ones, the intensely scorching ones, those who burn up this person's heart.

sanskrit: śocayābhi śocayā dīpayopa dīpaya | aher agne viṣaṃ tvaṃ tṛṇam iva kalvalaṃ daha ||
english: Scorch him through and through; scorch him, ignite and ignite him. O Agni, burn the serpent's venom like grass, along with his confusion.

sanskrit: sīdataṃ niṣattārāv avetaṃ mod gatam | kṛṣṇā vāṃ gauḥ sārasvatī ||
english: Sit down, O you two who are thoroughly seated; come back, go to where there is joy. The black cow of Sarasvatī is yours.

sanskrit: yathā rātrī kṛṣṇatamā gauḥ kṛṣṇā kṛṣṇavartaniḥ | śācīḥpyavo yathā rūpam evedaṃ māmakaṃ śiraḥ ||
english: As the darkest night, as a black cow with black tracks — as the appearance of those whose cheeks are streaked, so may this head of mine be.

sanskrit: yathāṅgaro 'bhiṣikto darvidāko yathāsitaḥ | anuṣyaṅgasya kalmaṣam evedaṃ māmakaṃ śiraḥ ||
english: As a charcoal anointed with oil, as a black ladle — may this head of mine be like the dark blemish of his successor.

sanskrit: yathā dāvād dahyamānāt kṛṣṇo jvālo 'padhvaṃsate | naiṣād asya yathā mukham evedaṃ māmakaṃ śiraḥ ||
english: As a black flame scatters from a burning forest fire — as the face of that Niṣāda, so may this head of mine be.

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cāsau manasā yac ca vācā yajñair juhoti haviṣā yajurbhiḥ | tan mṛtyunā nirṛtiḥ saṃvidānā purā dṛṣṭād ājyaṃ hantv asya ||
english: Whatever that one offers with mind or speech, with sacrifices, with oblations, with sacrificial formulas — may Nirṛti, allied with Death, destroy his oblation before it is seen.

sanskrit: yātudhānā nirṛtir ād u rakṣas te asya ghnantv anṛtena satyam | indreṣitā ājyam asya mathnantu mā tat saṃ pādi yad asau juhoti ||
english: The sorcerers, Nirṛti, and also the demons — let them strike down his truth with falsehood. Sent forth by Indra, let them churn up his oblation; may what that one offers not be fulfilled.

sanskrit: pari tvāgne puraṃ vayaṃ vipraṃ sahasya dhīmahi | dhṛṣadvarṇa divedive hantāraṃ bhaṅgurāvatām ||
english: O Agni, we set around you the inspired fort, O mighty one — you of bold color, day after day the slayer of the destroyers.

sanskrit: svarjid adhirājau śyenau saṃpātināv iva | ājyaṃ pṛtanyato hataṃ yo asmān pṛtanāyati ||
english: Two falcons that win the heavenly light, supreme rulers, swooping down together — the oblation of one who fights against us is destroyed, of whoever wages war against us.

sanskrit: pṛthivyai vanaspatibhya oṣadhībhyo 'gnaye 'dhipataye svāhā ||
english: Svāhā to the earth, to the forest trees, to the plants, to Agni the overlord.

sanskrit: antarikṣāya prāṇāya vayobhyo vāyave 'dhipataye svāhā ||
english: Svāhā to the atmosphere, to breath, to the birds, to Vāyu the overlord.

sanskrit: dive cakṣuṣe nakṣatrebhyaḥ sūryāyādhipataye svāhā ||
english: Svāhā to the sky, to the eye, to the asterisms, to Sūrya the overlord.

sanskrit: pippalyaḥ sam avadanta- -āyatīr jananād adhi | yaṃ jīvam aśnavāmahai na sa riṣyāti pūruṣaḥ ||
english: The pippalī plants have spoken together, coming forth from their origin: the man whom we living ones shall reach — he shall not be harmed.

sanskrit: pippalī kṣiptabheṣajy utāvaviddhabheṣajī | tāṃ devāḥ sam akalpayann alaṃ jīvātavā iti ||
english: The pippalī — remedy when thrown, and also remedy when pierced — the gods have fashioned her, saying: 'She is indeed sufficient for living.'

sanskrit: asurās tvā ny akhanan devās tvod avapan punaḥ | vātīkṛtasya bheṣajī pippalī kṣiptabheṣajī ||
english: The Asuras dug you down; the gods dug you up again. O pippalī, remedy when thrown, you are the healer of one afflicted by wind-sickness.

sanskrit: yad ulūko vadati mogham etad yat kapotaḥ padam agnau kṛṇoti | yasya dūtau prahitāv idam eyathus tasmai yamāya namo 'stu mṛtyave ||
english: When the owl hoots — that is futile; when the pigeon makes its mark in the fire — to Yama whose two messengers have been dispatched and have come here, homage be to him, to Death.

sanskrit: yas te dūto nirṛta ājagāma- -aprahitaḥ prahito vā gṛhaṃ naḥ | kapotolūkāv apadaṃ tad astv avairahatyam idam ā jagantha suvīratāyā idam ā sasattha ||
english: Whatever messenger of yours, O Nirṛti, has come — unsent or sent — to our house: let the pigeon and owl be footless in that. You have come here speaking of non-hostile slaying; you have settled here for the sake of good heroism.

sanskrit: yaḥ prathamaḥ pravata āsasāda bahubhyaḥ panthām anupaspaśānaḥ | ya īśe asya dvipado yaś catuṣpadas tasmai yamāya namo 'stu mṛtyave ||
english: He who first settled on the slope, searching out the path for the many — he who rules over this world's bipeds and quadrupeds — to that Yama, homage be, to Death.

sanskrit: yathāsitaḥ prathayate vaśām̐ anu vapūṃṣi kṛṇvann asurasya māyayā | evā me śepaḥ sahasāyam arka enāṅgena saṃsamakaṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: As the black one spreads out, following the cow, assuming forms through the Asura's magic — so may this hymn of my vigor, with this my member, make her fully equal to me.

sanskrit: yāvad aṅgīnaṃ pārasvataṃ hāstinaṃ gārdabhaṃ ca yat | yāvad aśvasya vājinas tāvan me vardhatāṃ pasaḥ ||
english: As great as the member of a creature with limbs, of a boar, of an elephant, of a donkey — as great as that of a powerful stallion — may my phallus grow to that size.

sanskrit: yathā pasas tāyādaraṃ vātena sthūlabhaṃ kṛtam | yāvat parasvataḥ pasas tāvan me vardhatāṃ pasaḥ ||
english: As the phallus of a certain one is made large and swollen by the wind — as great as the phallus of a boar — may my phallus grow to that size.
